audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Wukong 'immobile' and 'dash-less' and says three times that Nimbus Strike is 'his only gap-closer'. Warrior Trickster is also a dash, and it comes with invisibility. The entry mentions the clone but never the dash or the invisibility, so the reader is told to watch a decoy without being told the real Wukong has vanished at the same moment.
audit.why: Riot's text for Warrior Trickster: 'Wukong becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone that will attack nearby enemies', 275 range, 22/21/20/19/18s. Riot's text for Nimbus Strike: 'dashes to a targeted enemy', 650 range. Two dashes, not one. Also missing: Crushing Blow GAINS ATTACK RANGE (250 up to 350 by rank) and is an auto-attack reset — so the threat range is not his base auto range, and the tell is the wind-up rather than a visible cast.
audit.corrected: Nimbus Strike (E, 650 range, 10s) and Warrior Trickster (W, 22s) are both dashes, and W turns him invisible while the clone fights. Crushing Blow (Q, 8s) extends his auto range to 350 at rank 5, shreds armour, and opens with an auto-reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: Warrior Trickster is discussed twice with no cooldown, and Cyclone with no range.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is 22s at rank 1 — long enough that baiting it out genuinely buys a window. Cyclone is only 315 range, which is why a Comeuppance fired from 2500 beats it outright, and stating the number is what makes that claim land.
audit.corrected: W 22s at rank 1; Cyclone 315 range against a 2500-range Comeuppance.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry attributes his armour purely to items — 'he stacks armor and builds bruiser'. Stone Skin gives him stacking armour and max-health regeneration just from fighting, before any item exists.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Wukong gains stacking armor and max health regeneration while fighting champions and monsters.' That is why long exchanges get worse for a lethality champion as they go, independent of his build, and it is the mechanical reason to poke in short bursts rather than commit.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[2], wants.you[0] and late.

edits.before: Level 1 he just farms safely — don't facecheck for a fight with only Q and a single passive shot, concede it. Your window opens at 2-3: the second Dirty Fighting shot plus Avengerang lets you chip him for free if you hold him at boomerang range, because his only gap-closer is Nimbus Strike (E) and pre-3 he can't reach you to punish. Don't auto-walk into his armor-shred Q range — once he lands it he wants a point-blank brawl, and that's the one trade where your lethality poke does nothing.
edits.after: Level 1 he just farms safely — don't facecheck for a fight with only Q and a single passive shot, concede it. Your window opens at 2-3: the second Dirty Fighting shot plus Avengerang chips him for free at boomerang range, while neither of his dashes is ranked yet. Don't call him immobile though — Nimbus Strike (E) and Warrior Trickster (W) both close. And don't walk into Crushing Blow (Q): it EXTENDS his auto range to 350, shreds armour, and opens with an auto-reset, so the wind-up is the tell.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you keep poking, but respect that he now has E up as a gap-closer and the W clone as a juke — out-range his dash and never burn cooldowns on the decoy. At 6 it tips your way: Comeuppance locks on and executes off his missing health, so a poked Wukong dies from range before his Cyclone (R) reaches you, and any takedown refunds Heroic Swing to 0.5s for a free reset. But if he engages first and lands the R knockup, it locks you out of your E-swing escape and that's your death — whoever lands their key spell first wins the all-in.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you keep poking, but respect Nimbus Strike as a 650-range dash and Warrior Trickster as a 22s escape that turns him INVISIBLE while the clone fights on — never burn cooldowns on the decoy. At 6 it tips your way: Comeuppance executes off missing health from 2500, so a poked Wukong dies long before his 315-range Cyclone reaches you, and any takedown refunds Heroic Swing to 0.5s. But if he lands the R knockup first it locks you out of your swing escape — whoever lands their key spell first wins the all-in.

notes: The entry called Wukong 'immobile' and 'dash-less' and named Nimbus Strike as his only gap-closer three times. Warrior Trickster is a second dash AND grants invisibility — the page told the reader to watch the clone without ever saying the real Wukong disappears at that moment, which is the whole point of the ability. Also added Stone Skin, which the entry treated as an item property: he gains stacking armour just from fighting, so a lethality champion's long trades get worse the longer they run, before he buys anything. Crushing Blow's attack-range extension and auto-reset tell are in too. The packet's suspectName flag on wants.foe[0] ('Use Nimbus Strike') was a FALSE POSITIVE — the name is correct and the detector tripped on the preceding word. Note the kit file for this champion is champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json, not wukong.json.
